nieuw.titel: Trap ranked units by blocking their wheels
nieuw.tekst: Use Arcane Urgency to place a dragon in front of a ranked target, just close enough that the target's wheel would clip its base. Keep the target's sideways or turn-and-move escape within the dragon's charge arc, leaving it unable to escape the next charge through ordinary movement.
nieuw.waarom: He explains that blocking the wheel prevents the target from simply marching around the dragon. Leaving as much distance as the wheel block allows gives the dragon wider coverage of possible escapes.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He demonstrates trapping Chaos Knights, then a narrower chariot, by checking their sideways moves and their moves after turning each model.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He identifies Drilled, Arcane Urgency and Travel Mystical Pathways as possible escape tools. Narrower targets require more precise positioning.

nieuw.titel: Cover escape routes with a second threat

nieuw.waarom: He finds that mobile units, especially skirmishers or units with Arcane Urgency, can escape a single dragon's arc much more easily than two overlapping threats.

nieuw.titel: Screen landing space and leave room to wheel
nieuw.tekst: Against an Arcane Urgency dragon, deploy valuable cavalry back far enough to wheel, with chaff occupying the space in front. Fill the landing gaps so the dragon cannot park directly against the cavalry, then move the chaff aside to let the valuable unit escape.
nieuw.waarom: He says the dragon cannot charge on turn one, so denying its preferred landing position buys space for the valuable unit while only risking the chaff.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He places Chaos Knights well back, Chaos Warhounds on the deployment line and skirmishing Marauder Horsemen in another landing gap.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He says cavalry has the flexibility to get away, while infantry has much more difficulty. The screening units may also have to pass march tests.

nieuw.titel: Back a frontline wizard with a deterrent dragon
nieuw.tekst: If a wizard needs to stay on the front line, position your own dragon behind it to make an enemy dragon's attack risky. Cover the fight with a countercharge threat and check where an overrun or a retreat through your dragon would leave the attacker.
nieuw.waarom: He does not want his attacking dragon tied up against an evenly matched enemy dragon, and shows how the protective setup can leave him with unattractive choices whether he kills the wizard or not.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He places a Chaos Dragon behind a chariot-mounted sorcerer, covering a countercharge if the chariot gives ground and pre-measuring a Fall Back in Good Order through the friendly dragon.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He warns that the retreat must not carry the wizard off the board and that passing through the supporting dragon creates a panic risk. He sees no completely risk-free way to protect everything from an Arcane Urgency dragon.
